brief: A seven-cell honeycomb work surface, covered on top, with every open outside edge finished with caps.

requirements.evidence: Seven Hex base · Full pieces on level 0 in a flower layout: centre (0,0) plus all six neighbours (-1,0),(-1,1),(0,-1),(0,1),(1,-1),(1,0). The configurator reports no issues and meshClash is clear.
Seven full covers on the top face, one over each base (cover:*;full;top at each cell).

requirements.requirement: Every open outside edge finished with caps
requirements.evidence: capOpenFaces added 18 solid end caps on the perimeter faces of the outer ring; the interior faces are closed by neighbouring bases. Joints were locked with lockJoints (12 joint bolts).

finish.summary: Built a seven-cell honeycomb work surface: seven full hex bases on one level, arranged as a centre cell with six surrounding cells, each with a top cover. Open outside edges are closed with 18 caps, and the joints are bolted. check_build reports no issues and a clear mesh check. The build is a flat tabletop with no props or storage added, since the brief didn't ask for them.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
